title: A locally quasi-finite morphism with quasi-compact source has universally bounded fibres (Stacks 03JA)
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite], and assume $X$ is quasi-compact. Then the fibres of $f$ are universally bounded: there is an integer $n\geq0$ such that for every $y\in Y$ the fibre $X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ (fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product], residue field $\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-residue-field]) is a finite scheme over $\kappa(y)$, i.e. $X_y=\operatorname{Spec}B_y$ with $B_y$ a finite $\kappa(y)$-algebra, of degree $\dim_{\kappa(y)}B_y=\dim_{\kappa(y)}\Gamma(X_y,\mathcal O_{X_y})\leq n$; that is, $n$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $f$ and the fibres of $f$ are universally bounded [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound]. (Stacks Project, Morphisms, Definition Tag 03J4 and Lemma Tag 03JA.)

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03JA (lemma-locally-quasi-finite-qc-source-universally-bounded), line 15495; Definition Tag 03J4 (definition-universally-bounded), line 15302

proof.text: *Finite affine covering.* Since $X$ is quasi-compact, there are finitely many affine opens $U_1,\dots,U_m\subseteq X$ ($m\ge0$) covering $X$ and affine opens $V_1,\dots,V_m\subseteq Y$ with $f(U_i)\subseteq V_i$: for each $x\in X$ choose an affine open $V_x\ni f(x)$ of $Y$ and an affine open $U_x\ni x$ of $X$ contained in the open $f^{-1}(V_x)$ (affine opens form a basis of the topology of a scheme [def-pc-scheme]); the $U_x$ cover $X$, and quasi-compactness gives finitely many of them covering $X$. (The affine opens form a basis: [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis].)

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03JA, first paragraph, lines 15505-15518

proof.text: *The pieces are quasi-finite.* Let $f_i=f|_{U_i}:U_i\to V_i$ be the restriction ($\iota_{V_i}\circ f_i=f\circ\iota_{U_i}$ for the inclusions of the open subschemes). By the local nature of local quasi-finiteness [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-restriction-to-opens] (Stacks 01TH (4)), $f_i$ is locally quasi-finite. As a morphism between affine schemes, $f_i$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], hence quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] (3). A locally quasi-finite quasi-compact morphism is quasi-finite [pqf-lem-qf-locqf-qc] (Stacks 01TJ). So each $f_i$ is a quasi-finite morphism of affine schemes.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03JA, first paragraph, lines 15505-15518 (with Lemmas Tag 01TH (4) and 01TJ)

proof.text: For a finite morphism g:Z→Spec A, Z is affine and B=Γ(Z,⊤) is a finite A-module under g's structure map [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], using IsFinite.finite_appTop and RingHom.finite_algebraMap. For each y, with residue field κ(y) [def-weil-residue-field], Spec.map_surjective expresses the residue-field point as Spec of a map A→κ(y). The affine pullback section isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies Γ(Z_y,⊤) as a κ(y)-algebra with κ(y)⊗_A B. Set n to the minimal number of A-module generators of B. Mathlib Submodule.FG.spanFinrank_baseChange_le (Mathlib/Algebra/Module/SpanRankOperations.lean:43) gives that the minimal number of generators of the tensor product is at most n; over a field this number is the dimension, by Module.finrank_eq_spanFinrank_of_free (Mathlib/Algebra/Module/SpanRank.lean:448). Finiteness of the fibre projection follows from base change of IsFinite. Thus n bounds the fibres of g. For a general affine target V, apply this to g followed by V.isoSpec.hom and compose with V.isoSpec.inv, whose bound is one [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-fibre-degree-one; lem-weil-pbc-composition-fibre-degree-bound]; the composite equals g. These are the proved private helpers finite_spec_bound and finite_affine_bound.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03JA, third paragraph, lines 15537-15552

proof.text: *Quasi-finite morphisms of affine schemes.* Let $g:U\to V$ be a quasi-finite morphism of affine schemes. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-affine-open-in-finite] (Stacks 03GU) there are an affine scheme $Z$, an open immersion $j:U\to Z$ and a finite morphism $\pi:Z\to V$ with $g=\pi\circ j$. The open immersion $j$ is an immersion (the identity of $U$, a closed immersion, followed by $j$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]), so $1$ bounds the degrees of its fibres [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-fibre-degree-one] (Stacks 03J9). By step 3 some integer $n$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $\pi$. By [lem-weil-pbc-composition-fibre-degree-bound] (Stacks 03J6) the integer $1\cdot n=n$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $g=\pi\circ j$. Applied to the morphisms $f_i$ of step 2, this gives integers $n_i\ge0$ such that $n_i$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $f_i:U_i\to V_i$ [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound]. Then compose f_i with the target-open immersion V_i→Y, whose fibres have degree at most one, using the same immersion and composition lemmas. The equation resLE_comp_ι identifies this composite with U_i→X→Y. Hence each map U_i→Y has a bound n_i. This removes the need to identify the residue fields of V_i and Y separately.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03JA, second paragraph, lines 15521-15535 (Lemmas Tag 03GU, 03J9, 03J6)

proof.text: Fix y∈Y and let W_i=(f.fiberι y)^{-1}(U_i). The preimage_iSup identity shows that the W_i cover X_y. The restriction square from isPullback_morphismRestrict [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product] has horizontal maps W_i→U_i and X_y→X. Paste it vertically with the defining fibre square [def-pc-scheme-fibre; lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting]. The resulting square says W_i, with its map to Spec κ(y) given by W_i→X_y→Spec κ(y), is the fibre of U_i→Y at y. Its canonical isoPullback commutes with this map by isoPullback_hom_snd. Transport the IsFinite instance and the finrankΓ bound from step 4 across that source isomorphism (finrankΓ_eq_of_iso with identity base isomorphism). This is the proved private helper bounds_of_open_cover; no case distinction on y∈V_i and no residue-field naturality are needed.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03JA, first paragraph, lines 15505-15518 ('For $y \in Y$ it is clear that $X_y = \bigcup_{y \in V_i} (U_i)_y$ is an open covering')

proof.text: Apply finite_open_cover_degree_sum [lem-weil-pbc-finite-open-cover-degree-sum] to X_y→Spec κ(y), the opens W_i, and the bounds n_i transported in step 5. It yields both IsFinite of the fibre projection and its finrankΓ≤∑_i n_i, including the empty-cover case. The same sum works for every y and hence witnesses HasUniversallyBoundedFibers f [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound]. The finite cover is indexed by Fin s.card using s.equivFin, where s is the finite subcover selected in step 1.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03JA, first paragraph, lines 15505-15518 ('if $n_i$ works for the morphism $f|_{U_i}$, then $\sum n_i$ works for $f$')

Proof follows the three paragraphs of the Stacks proof in six steps: finite affine cover with f(U_i) in V_i (elementary); f|U_i: U_i -> V_i quasi-finite (new node lem-weil-pbc-lqf-restriction-to-opens for 01TH (4); pqf-def-affine-morphism, lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence (3) for quasi-compactness; pqf-lem-qf-locqf-qc for 01TJ, an off-route tool already accepted by L on lem-weil-pbc-flat-fp-qf-stratification); the finite case written out (fibre Spec(B tensor kappa(p)) via existing Mathlib-leaf nodes, generators give the bound); the quasi-finite affine case via new nodes for 03GU (open immersion into a finite affine Z), 03J9 (immersions: bound 1) and 03J6 (bounds multiply under composition); the identification of the fibres (U_i)_y with the open subschemes p^{-1}(U_i) of X_y written out with the open-preimage and pasting leaves; and the summation, which Stacks states without proof, as the new node lem-weil-pbc-finite-open-cover-degree-sum (agent-stated, source the 03JA proof and the Artinian arguments of 03J5/03J6). Tags 03J4, 03J6, 03J9, 03JA, 03GU, 01TH, 01TJ, 01TD, 00QB verified in stacks-project/tags/tags.
